classification.difficultyReason: Factor a difference of squares, apply the taught absolute-value split and sketch two restricted linear branches with open endpoints.

answer.short:
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}x+1,&x>1,\\-x-1,&x<1.\end{cases}$$
Undefined at $x=1$. The graph has open endpoints at $(1,2)$ and $(1,-2)$.
answer.worked:
The denominator is zero at $x=1$, so $x\ne1$.
$$\begin{aligned}x^2-1&=(x-1)(x+1).\end{aligned}$$
For $x>1$, $|x-1|=x-1$:
$$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{x-1}\\f(x)&=x+1.\end{aligned}$$
For $x<1$, $|x-1|=-(x-1)$:
$$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=\frac{(x-1)(x+1)}{-(x-1)}\\f(x)&=-(x+1)\\f(x)&=-x-1.\end{aligned}$$
Sketch $y=x+1$ for $x>1$ and $y=-x-1$ for $x<1$. Mark open endpoints at $(1,2)$ and $(1,-2)$. The left branch crosses the $y$-axis at $-1$.

spec.description: Two blue rays with open endpoints at (1,-2) and (1,2), black axes, a horizontal dashed guide at y=2 and a vertical dashed guide between the endpoints. Only y=2 and y=-1 are numerically labelled; x=1 remains unlabelled.
spec.mathematics: y=-x-1 for x<1; y=x+1 for x>1; undefined at x=1.
